questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Integration Testing Express Routes?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Tests should exercise success paths, invalid inputs, permissions, boundary conditions, and dependency failures. Keep external side effects isolated and run repeatable checks in CI before deployment.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.

questions.prompt: A change related to Integration Testing Express Routes appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.

Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
